This first part of the protocol is aimed to prepare the Collagen from rat tail tendon. If your lab already has collagen suitable for 3D matrix polymerization, you may skip this step. Collagen Type I solution from rat tail Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #C3867 (CAS: 9007-34-5) Please cite: Rajan, N., Habermehl, J., Coté, M.-F., Doillon, C. J. & Mantovani, D. steps.title: Thaw and Wash Rat Tails
steps.instruction: Prepare rat tails for collagen extraction by thawing and cleaning.

substeps.instruction: Remove 10-15 rat tails from -80 °C and thaw at 4 °C for 24 hours.
Move tails from 4 °C to room temperature for 30 minutes.
Wash tails in ultrapure water in a large beaker, then transfer to a second beaker with fresh ultrapure water.

steps.title: Extract Collagen Fibers
steps.instruction: Mechanically isolate collagen fibers from the rat tail skin.

substeps.instruction: Dry a single tail with a paper towel.
Hold the tail 5 mm from the thinner end with tweezers and twist the tail around the tweezers until the skin breaks.
Pull the tweezers to extract the collagen fibers.
Cut the fibers and immerse them in room temperature 1X PBS; repeat until the tail is processed.
Transfer fibers to new PBS for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Purify and Solubilize Fibers
steps.instruction: Clean the fibers and dissolve them in acetic acid.

substeps.instruction: Transfer fibers to a beaker with 500 mL of PBS and wait 5 minutes.
Transfer fibers to 500 mL of pure acetone (inside a chemical hood) until flexibility is lost.
Transfer fibers to 500 mL of 70% Isopropanol (350 mL isopropanol and 150 mL ultrapure water) for 5 minutes.
Collect fibers in a large beaker using a magnetic bar and add 500 mL of 20 mM acetic acid (574 µL glacial acetic acid in 500 mL ultrapure water).
Stir for at least 48 hours at 4 °C; add more 20 mM acetic acid if the solution becomes too dense.

steps.title: Homogenize and Freeze Collagen
steps.instruction: Process the viscous collagen solution into a frozen state.

substeps.instruction: Prepare small pieces of ultrapure water ice and store a blender and centrifuge flasks at 4 °C.
Transfer the collagen solution and ice to the blender; pulse multiple times to keep the solution cold (4 °C) until it becomes pale white.
Transfer the solution to centrifuge flasks, balance them, and immediately wash the blender.
Transfer the solution (without disturbing the pellet) to plastic or metallic containers to form an ice layer thinner than 5 mm.
Store at -20 °C for 48 hours until completely frozen.

steps.title: Lyophilize and Store Collagen
steps.instruction: Remove water from the collagen to create a stable sponge.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 10,000 x g for 1 hour at 4 °C.
Remove frozen collagen, crush into smaller pieces, and transfer to a freeze-dryer flask.
Perform lyophilization for 96 hours, thawing the condenser coil if necessary.
Remove the resulting collagen sponge, transfer to ziplock bags, and store at -80 °C.

steps.title: Reconstitute and Dialyze Collagen
steps.instruction: Dissolve the collagen sponge and remove impurities.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 5 L of 20 mM acetic acid and store at 4 °C.
Weigh the desired amount of collagen sponge (suggested 4 mg/mL) into a beaker flask.
Add 20 mM acetic acid to reach the desired concentration and dissolve using a hand blender.
Perform dialysis against 20 mM acetic acid (1:10 ratio) at 4 °C for 2 hours.
Change the dialysis buffer and leave overnight at 4 °C with a magnetic bar.

steps.title: Sterilize Collagen Solution
steps.instruction: Use chloroform to sterilize the solubilized collagen.

substeps.instruction: Transfer dialyzed collagen to a sterile borosilicate glass flask with a lid.
Carefully add chloroform (10% of total collagen volume) to the bottom of the flask without mixing.
Incubate for 24 hours at 4 °C.
Using aseptic technique in a biological safety cabinet, remove the chloroform.
Leave the flask open on ice for 1 hour to remove chlorine gas.
Test for sterility and store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Coat 96-Well Plates
steps.instruction: Prepare and apply the collagen coating to the plate.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the Collagen COATING solution on ice using pre-cooled tips (4 °C): mix 450.0 μL of Collagen I (4 mg/mL stock to reach 0.3 mg/mL) with 5.6 mL of 20 mmol/L Acetic Acid (Total 6 mL).
Briefly vortex and spin the conical tube.
Dispense 50 µL of coating solution into each well of a 96-well plate and rock gently to ensure even coating.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C, 5% CO2 for 1 hour.
Aspirate the solution and wash twice with PBS.
Dry the plate in the hood, seal, and store at 4 °C or use immediately.

steps.title: Seed Cells and Incubate
steps.instruction: Seed the target cell lines onto the coated plates.

substeps.instruction: Tripsinize and count cells (e.g., using a Neubauer chamber).
Prepare a cell suspension in 100 µL per well based on suggested cell numbers.
Allow the plate to sit at room temperature for 5 minutes for even dispersion.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C, 5% CO2 for 12 to 24 hours.

steps.title: Perform Scratch Assay
steps.instruction: Create a wound in the cell monolayer and prepare for invasion.

substeps.instruction: Remove medium and wash cells with serum-free medium.
Add 150 µL of serum-free medium supplemented with 0.1% HI-BSA.
Incubate at 37 °C, 5% CO2 for 12 to 24 hours.
Perform scratches in all wells (e.g., using Gilson's Aspiration Station Kit accessory 4 or 5 with 200 µL tips) and verify via microscope.
Remove medium with a multichannel pipette and wash once with serum-free medium.
Add 100 μL of serum-free medium to the wells.
Place the plate over ice (covered with aluminum foil) for 5 minutes.
Remove the medium.

steps.title: Apply 3D Matrix and Medium
steps.instruction: Overlay the scratch with collagen and growth medium.

substeps.instruction: Overlay each well with 50 μL of Collagen INVADING solution and rock gently.
Overlay the 3D matrices with 100 μL of pre-warmed medium containing 10% FBS (or 25 mM HEPES-Buffered media).
Add an additional 200 µL of medium supplemented with 10% FBS (or 25 mM HEPES-Buffered media).

steps.title: Image and Analyze Results
steps.instruction: Capture time-lapse images and process data using ImageJ scripts.

substeps.instruction: Immediately image the plate at 0h using an Operetta system (10X Long WD objective, Brightfield, 15% overlap, 9 fields per well in square-shape) at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
Perform readings every hour for 24 hours.
Export images from Columbus as 'Single Plane Tiff' and remove all accessory files (e.g., .csv and .xml index files).
Run ImageJ script 'Scratch_and_Wound_1-Sorter_n_Tiler_v0.3_overlap_mult.ijm'.
Rename the resulting 'Tiles' folder to 'TimepointBegin' (for 0H) or 'TimepointEnd' (for other timepoints).
Organize folders for each timepoint containing one 'TimepointBegin' and one 'TimepointEnd' folder.
Run ImageJ script 'Scratch_and_Wound_2-Measure_v0.4.ijm' (or v0.2.1) for final measurement.
